### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4b83b3b2a06da6dfcbafc5bb98facc97b3c4aeb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fbc6c5ad90d0486f686e7822ac61f698208d32f0`

### ① Derived judgments

Reviewed against merge-base `a675ad4ef0` and, for the queue leg, a no-commit merge with `origin/main` `0046a41b43`. Every number below was re-run in a detached worktree of the head sha; nothing was taken from the PR body except where ③ says so.

1. **New exported const `UNPROJECTABLE_BRANCHES_KEY`** in `packages/spec/scripts/lib/union-branch-projection.ts` — public surface unchanged. `packages/spec/package.json` `files[]` is `dist, json-schema, liveness, prompts, llms.txt, README.md, src/**/*.zod.ts, CHANGELOG.md, api-surface, api-surface-declarations, spec-changes.json`; `scripts/` is not in it. All 22 `tsup.config.ts` entries are under `src/`, and no non-test `src/` file imports this module, so no byte of it reaches `dist`. `git grep` of the name over `api-surface/`, `api-surface-declarations/` and `src/` at head: 0 hits. **Right.**
2. **New exported function `auditUnprojectableBranchRecord`** — same module, same reach: 0 hits on every published path. **Right.**
3. **New required field `unpruned` on the exported interface `BranchProjection`** — same module. The only constructor is `projectByPruningUnionBranches` (sets it from a `structuredClone` taken before the prune); the only consumers at head are `build-schemas.ts` and the test file, both readers. `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.scripts.json` exit 0. **Right.**
4. **Writer literal replaced by the constant** (`build-schemas.ts` line 558) — same value. The emitted key is carried by 6 files at base and at head; the accept set of every emitted schema is unchanged (see ② for the byte diff). **Right.**
5. **Guard rewritten to `branchProjection` plus the positive `prunedBranches.length` check** — the two conditions cannot disagree: both are assigned from the same `projected` value (lines 537–538), `projectByPruningUnionBranches` returns null when nothing was pruned (module line 492), and neither variable is assigned anywhere else. No path skips the audit for a pruned projection, and none audits a schema whose record was not written: the write is two statements above the read in the same block. The audit's absent/empty-record arm is therefore unreachable from this call site (live only for the unit tests). **Right.**
6. **New fatal path in `gen:schema`** (a disagreeing record now exits 1 — a narrowing of the BUILD's accept set, not of any published contract). Judged as unable to red `main` or an unrelated PR, on three legs.
   - *Faithful replay.* `markedUnionMembers` walks exactly the node set `pruneMarkedUnionBranches` walks (arrays, then every object entry, then `anyOf`/`oneOf`); the prune records pre-removal indices at every level because it recurses into children before it splices the parent; the replay removes deepest pointer first and, within one depth, highest index first, so no removal shifts a pointer not yet applied. Executed probes against the head module, all 0 defects: prefix pointers (`#/anyOf/0` together with `#/anyOf/0/anyOf/0` and `#/anyOf/0/anyOf/1`), siblings at different depths under one parent array (`#/anyOf/0` with `#/anyOf/1/anyOf/1`; `#/anyOf/0/anyOf/1` with `#/anyOf/2`), three of five in one container, each of those with the record handed in reversed, one Zod union reused at two properties (Zod emits distinct JS objects per site, `a === b` false, so the completeness sweep cannot over-report a shared node), a reused union with `id` metadata (hoisted to `$defs`, pointer `#/$defs/…/anyOf/1`), and RFC 6901 escaped keys (`a~1b`, `c~0d`). No counterexample.
   - *Carve-out vs the writer's real key list.* Read off `build-schemas.ts` at head, lines 544–561: before the audit runs the writer sets exactly `$id`, `x-spec-version`, `x-io` (input direction only) and the record; `x-dropped-refinements` is set after the audit (line 583 onward) and is outside its view. All four are covered by the `$id` / `x-` rule. The one root key not carved out, `$schema`, is emitted by Zod into the projection itself (present in both trees) and the per-file writer never touches it. The `not in replay` clause could misfire only on a projection whose root already carries `$id` or one of those `x-` names: Zod emits no `$id` from `id` metadata (probe above), and `src/` carries no `x-` metadata and none of those names (0 hits).
   - *Measured.* `gen:schema` at head: exit 0, 1541 schemas, 5 projected, 31 branches, 0 record defects — twice, byte-identical output. At base: exit 0. On the no-commit merge with `origin/main` `0046a41b43` (which changed `refinement-projection.ts` to emit `propertyNames`/`allOf` inside the projection, plus 44 other spec files, no conflict): exit 0, 1542 schemas, same 5 projections, 0 defects. Ablation: writer tampered to `prunedBranches.slice(1)` (blob moved, restore proved equal to HEAD) — `gen:schema` exit 1 naming 5 records. **Right.**
7. **Seven new pins** — non-vacuity measured by mutating the reader, each mutation anchor-counted onto disk and restored to the HEAD blob: delete the completeness sweep, 3 red of 28; neuter the replay comparison, 1 red; neuter the mark-mismatch check, 1 red; drop the deepest-first sort, 1 red; invert the sort, 1 red. `publish()` re-spells the writer's `map`, but the audit reads only `published` and `projection.unpruned` (a clone taken before the prune) and never `projection.schema`, so spread-versus-in-place cannot change its inputs; the in-place real writer is exercised by every `gen:schema`, and by the ablation above. **Right**, one wording nit under ③.

### ② Semver level

**None owed.** No published symbol, key, value or schema file moves; the three changed files are outside `files[]` and outside every entry point.

- `Clause-②: no` — **consistent.** The direction is a refusal added to the build, not a widening of any accept set or of the public surface. `node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff pr.diff`, verbatim: `✓ check-widening-tells: 3 changed file(s) — 0 judged against a declared surface (no widening tell), 3 NOT MEASURED. ⛔ NOTHING on this diff was examined for widening tells, so this exit 0 is evidence about no surface at all.` followed by `no declared surface covers it (3)` naming the three files. Read as: the surfaces that instrument polices were not touched; the surface judgment above is mine, from `files[]`, the entries and the api-surface artifacts.
- `skip-changeset` — **consistent, with one correction to the PR's prose.** I ran the byte-for-byte BASE-vs-HEAD diff of the emitted `json-schema/` tree the PR said it did not run: 1532 files each side; all 1531 schema files byte-identical; the ONE differing file is `json-schema/.build-input-hash-schema` (65 bytes), the freshness stamp the generator writes from a hash of its own inputs (`scripts/build-input-hash.mjs`, read only by `schemaTreeIsStale`). A head-vs-head rerun is identical, so the move is PR-caused. The stamp does ship in the tarball (npm pack listing, beside `dist/.build-input-hash*`), moves on every generator edit, and moved identically on #18618 (same file, `skip-changeset`, merged). A receipt of which inputs built the tree is not a published contract; the label stands. The PR body's "emitted output is unchanged" is exact for every schema and inexact for the stamp.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dispatch fences (5736682927), each verified from the diff:** a reader was built (fence 1); the published field is still written — 6 files carry it at head (fence 2); the PR states its four reasons for the checking reader over the docs page, which the adjudication 5733358188 named as a legitimate reader (fence 3); the card-sentence correction is carried forward (fence 4); counts were re-derived here with the instrument's own lit output (fence 5); `content/docs/references/**` is untouched — the diff is three files under `packages/spec/scripts/` (fence 6); no governed surface on the file list (fence 7); `Clause-②: no` measured, above (fence 8).
- **`Fixes #17107` with the docs half unbuilt** — consistent with the adjudication (a checking reader is a reader; the docs page is the card's example, not the definition). Follow-up for the seat, not a defect: the rendering of `x-unprojectable-branches` into `filter.mdx` / `hook.mdx` is neither built nor filed; either file it as its own card (it is a `merge=os-regen` tree change) or record on the card that artifact-only reach is intended. The PR leaves that choice open and says so.
- **`x-io` has zero readers** (dev report 5737162721) — escalated to the seat's routing, not this PR's: a published field, so the enforce-or-remove channel per 5732887703.
- **`check-clause2-carriers --pair 19135`** — live run exit 4 on **C6 only** (no `## Contract review` record on this head); this comment is that record. C8 is clean: `claim.repeat: none`, the older claim 5643709338 read as RETRACTED by 5737191680.
- **Base moved.** `main` `0046a41b43` touched `refinement-projection.ts` and 44 other spec files since `a675ad4ef0`; none of the PR's three files; merged generation green (① item 6). The queue rebuild re-runs it.
- **Wording nit, non-blocking:** the pin titled "accepts the record build-schemas.ts actually writes" audits the record `publish()` writes; the real writer is pinned by the build itself and by the ablation above. Optional follow-up: a spawned-generator case in `build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` with the writer tampered.
- **Not re-run here, taken from CI at this head:** the repo-wide eslint sweep (`Lint & Repo Gates` success) and the full spec test suite (`Test Core` success). All seven required contexts read `success` at `fbc6c5ad90`.
